questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Does she know me?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Am I known to her'?**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence '**Does she know me ?' **is in **active **voice and it is an interrogatory sentence.
 
• We need to convert it into active voice.
 
• The subject of the passive voice becomes the object of the active voice and vice versa.
 
• **She **becomes **her **and **me **become **I** after the conversion.
 
• Convert '**know**' into the third form of its verb i.e. **Known**.
 
• The verb '**known**' takes a fixed preposition '**to**' after it.
 
• Hence, after following the rules of conversion, the passive voice is - **Am I known to her ?**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **option 4.**

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Dozens of distinctly different regional languages are spoken in India, which share many characteristics such as grammatical structure and vocabulary.

B. India has had a longer exposure to English than any other country which uses it as a second language, its distinctive words, idioms, grammar and rhetoric spreading gradually to affect all places, habits and culture.

C. The historical background of India is never far away from everyday usage of English.

D. Since the early 1600s, the English language has had a toehold on the Indian subcontinent, when the East India Company established settlements in Chennai, Kolkata, and Mumbai, formerly Madras, Calcutta, and Bombay, respectively.
questions.solution:
The correct order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph is:

DBCA

Sentence D introduces the historical background of English language in India, and sentence B adds to it by mentioning how the English language has spread its influence in the country. Sentence C follows up with the idea that this influence can still be seen in everyday English usage in India. Finally, sentence A concludes the paragraph by pointing out that despite the regional linguistic diversity in India, there are some common characteristics that the languages share.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

The ministry officials

P. recommend the shortlisted names to

Q. the awards selection committee

R. sieve through the applicants' credentials and

S. have been working overtime to
questions.solution:
The correct order of the parts of the sentence is:

SRPQ

The correct sentence would be: "The ministry officials have been working overtime to sieve through the applicants' credentials and recommend the shortlisted names to the awards selection committee."

The sentence talks about the process of shortlisting candidates for an award. To make the sentence coherent, it is important to arrange the parts of the sentence in the correct order.

The first part of the sentence is "have been working overtime to," which indicates the continuous effort made by the ministry officials. This is followed by "sieve through the applicants' credentials," which describes the process of scrutinizing the qualifications of the candidates.

Then comes "recommend the shortlisted names to," which explains the ultimate goal of the ministry officials' effort. Finally, the sentence ends with "the awards selection committee," which indicates the recipient of the shortlisted names.

Therefore, the correct order of the parts of the sentence is SRPQ, which results in the sentence: "The ministry officials have been working overtime to sieve through the applicants' credentials and recommend the shortlisted names to the awards selection committee."

• We need to substitute the underlined segment with one of the options :
 
• ** 'Neither,nor,so**' follows the inversion in which the **auxiliary verb comes** before the subject than the main verb.
 
 
• ***Example: **She does not want to be constricted by narrow feminism **nor does she** accept the cultural burden handed to her as a woman.*

• **In this case, 'nor does she smile' is the correct structure** for the following statement.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** option 3.**

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

Anita said to the mother, “Your child has been crying since morning.”

options.text: Anita told the mother that her child was crying since morning.
Anita told the mother that her child had been crying since morning.
Anita told the mother that her child had been cry since morning.
Anita told the mother that your child had been crying since morning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Anita told the mother that her child had been crying since morning.'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in*** direct speech.***
 
• ***We ****need to convert it into **Indirect Speech.***
 
• The rules of conversion are :
 
• Reporting verb **'Said to**' is coverted to **'Told'.**
 
• ** Commas** and** Inverted commas** will be replaced with 'that'.
 
• If **personal pronouns** are there in the reported speech,it will be changed according to the** subject** and the **object **of the **reporting verb .**
 
• If the sentence is in **Present Perfect Progressive** in** Direct speech**, then it will change to** Past perfect progressive** in **Indirect speech.**
 
 
• **Structure **: ** has/have+** *been+ V1+ing (direct*) to ***had +been + V1+ing (indirect)***
 
 
 
• ***​***Finally,we will get the final sentence, '***Anita told the mother that her child had been crying since morning'.*__**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 2.**
